title: Variable value table
subject: Computing
unit: Spring 1: Variables in games and e-bullying
source: Seeded from computing/y6 lesson 5 (Variable value table (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 5: What is a variable? Score and lives. To understand that a variable stores a value that can change while a program runs

questions.q: Start: score 0. Catch, catch, catch. What is score?
questions.model: Teacher writes the value after each event: 0, 1, 2, 3.

questions.q: Start: lives 3. Miss, miss. What is lives?
What is the difference between 'set score to 0' and 'change score by 1'?
questions.a: Set replaces the value; change adds to it.

questions.q: Core: Make a new Scratch project with a Bowl sprite and an Apple sprite (delete the cat). Create the variables score and lives and set them on green flag.
questions.a: set score to 0, set lives to 3 on green flag.
questions.model: Teacher makes 'score', sets it to 0, then pupils make 'lives'.

questions.q: Extend: Fill a value table for 6 events of your own (catch or miss).
questions.a: Any table where score goes up by 1 on a catch and lives down by 1 on a miss.

questions.q: Stretch: What should happen when lives reaches 0? Write it as an if... then rule.
questions.a: IF lives = 0 THEN say 'Game over' and stop all.

questions.q: A variable... A) never changes B) stores a value that can change C) is a sprite
questions.a: B) stores a value that can change
options: Stores a value that can change

questions.q: Name two variables a game might use.
